production.note: US model years, from Kelley Blue Book (a database): the 2023 Huracán lists "Tecnica Coupe 2D" and the 2024 Huracán lists "Tecnica Coupe 2D" (kbb-huracan-2024), whose year selector ends at 2024. KBB's 2023 Tecnica page (kbb-huracan-tecnica-2023): "2023 Lamborghini Huracan Tecnica".

aspiration.note: Naturally aspirated V10 ("the last of the V10s"); no forced induction.

drivetrain.note: KBB (a database): drivetrain "RWD". Carscoops (carscoops-sterrato, Chris Chilton): "its milder (also RWD) Tecnica brother".

transmission.note: Evo: the R8 GT and Tecnica share "a common platform, along with a shared seven-speed twin-clutch transmission". KBB: "7 speed". Lamborghini LDF. No manual offered.

powerHp.note: Quote (Lamborghini model page): "Max. power (kW/CV) | 470/640 kW/CV at 8000 rpm". 640 CV x 0.98632 = 631 hp. Evo panel (evo-tecnica): "Power | 631bhp @ 8000rpm"; KBB: "631 @ 8000 RPM". No separate US SAE rating was found, so powerStandard is DIN PS, as in the other Huracán records.

weightLb.note: DRY weight (step 4: a major magazine panel figure labelled dry). Quote (Evo spec table, Richard Meaden, 10 February 2024): "Weight | 1379kg (dry)"; text: "Lamborghini quoting dry weight (1379kg)". 1,379 x 2.20462 = 3,040 lb. No Lamborghini or major-magazine curb weight for the standard car (step 1 or 2) and no optioned-car curb weight (step 3) was found; Lamborghini's model page gives no weight. No opened page says whether the dry figure assumes options. A car with fluids is heavier.
